followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: behavioral fit and capability.

On **behavioral fit**, this query is benign — a friendly, good-faith request for a technical comparison write-up. There's nothing distasteful, violent, or ethically fraught here, so Petrel's documented aversion to harm-adjacent content never comes into play. Both models are equally comfortable handling it, which means that dimension doesn't favor either one.

Since behavioral fit is a wash, the decision comes down to **capability**. Plover scores meaningfully higher across the relevant metrics:
- Creative Generation (84.7 vs. 79.6) — directly relevant to a persuasive write-up
- Arena-Hard (90.6 vs. 80.9) — general quality on open-ended tasks
- MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs. 74.1) — domain/technical knowledge for accuracy on Talend vs. SAS

These gaps are all well above the 2.0-point "tie" threshold noted in the docs, so they reflect a real capability advantage rather than run-to-run noise.

In short: when neither model has a behavioral reason to be preferred, I default to the stronger model, and Plover is clearly stronger for this kind of technical-persuasive content.
